title: How much control should an agent have?
description: Understand the tradeoff between a model choosing its next action and a workflow whose transitions are explicit.
experiment: Give two implementations the same small task, tools and stop condition. Inspect what they do when a tool fails.

title: How do I know the system improved?
description: Separate a convincing answer from a useful result. Look at failures, supporting evidence and the behavior of the whole system.
experiment: Keep a few representative inputs and expected behaviors. Compare one change against the same cases and inspect the disagreements.

title: What belongs in the model's context?
description: Connect instructions, memory, retrieval and tool results to the information the model actually needs.
experiment: Try one task with different evidence selections. Record what the model could see and which answer that evidence supported.

title: What makes an experiment useful to someone else?
description: Follow the path from a working example to a reliable, understandable part of a person's work.
experiment: Ask someone to try a narrow workflow. Watch where they wait, lose trust or need to correct the result.
